category: Cloud III: Sockets, URL & HTTP Functions, Mail, Web Automation & API Details
description: Low-level networking (sockets, IP and host lookup), URL parsing and encoding, HTTP response construction and redirects for deployed APIs, request/response details of APIFunction and FormFunction, mail sending and reading, browser automation with WebExecute, web and Wikipedia search, and interactive question flows with AskFunction.

tools.name: SocketConnect
tools.description: Opens a TCP (or ZeroMQ) client connection to host:port, returning a SocketObject that acts as a stream: WriteString/BinaryWrite send bytes and ReadString/ReadByteArray/SocketReadMessage receive them. Use it to talk to instruments, custom servers and protocols that have no higher-level Wolfram interface.
tools.usage:
socket = SocketConnect["host:port"]
socket = SocketConnect[{"host", port}, "TCP"]
socket = SocketConnect["tcp://host:port", "ZMQ_REQ"]
WriteString[socket, "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n"]
SocketReadMessage[socket]
Close[socket]
tools.notes: SocketReadyQ tests for pending data; Sockets[] lists open sockets.

tools.name: SocketListen
tools.description: Starts a server that listens on a port (or a SocketObject from SocketOpen) and calls a handler function for each incoming connection/message with an association containing "Data", "SourceSocket", "Timestamp" etc.; returns a SocketListener that can be stopped with DeleteObject. Setting the handler to respond with an HTTP response turns it into a minimal local web server.
tools.usage:
listener = SocketListen[port, handler]
listener = SocketListen[SocketOpen[port], handler]
SocketListen[port, handler, HandlerFunctionsKeys -> {"Data", "SourceSocket"}]
DeleteObject[listener]
SocketOpen[port]
SocketOpen[{"host", port}, "TCP"]

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Function receiving the event association; write replies to #SourceSocket.

tools.example:
srv = SocketListen[8080, Function[{assoc},
   With[{s = assoc["SourceSocket"]},
    WriteString[s, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello"]; Close[s]]]];
URLRead["http://localhost:8080"]["Body"]
DeleteObject[srv]
tools.notes: For production HTTP endpoints deploy APIFunction to the cloud instead; SocketListen is for local tools and device protocols.

tools.name: SocketReadMessage
tools.description: Reads a complete message (all currently available bytes, or one ZeroMQ frame) from a socket as a ByteArray; SocketWriteMessage sends a ByteArray or string, SocketReadyQ tests whether data is waiting (optionally with a timeout), and Sockets lists open sockets. Together with ReadString/WriteString they give both message- and stream-oriented socket I/O.
tools.usage:
SocketReadMessage[socket]
SocketReadMessage[socket, n]
SocketWriteMessage[socket, msg]
SocketReadyQ[socket]
SocketReadyQ[socket, timeout]
Sockets[]

tools.name: IPAddress
tools.description: IPAddress["1.2.3.4"] represents an IP address (with IPv6 support and address arithmetic); HostLookup resolves host names to addresses (and reverse lookups), PingTime measures round-trip time to a host, URLResponseTime the time to fetch a URL, and $MachineAddresses / $NetworkInterfaces / $NetworkConnected describe the local network state. Use them for connectivity diagnostics in scripts.
tools.usage:
IPAddress["192.168.0.1"]
HostLookup["host"]
HostLookup["host", "IPv6"]
HostLookup[IPAddress["8.8.8.8"]]
PingTime["host"]
PingTime["host", n]
URLResponseTime[url]
$MachineAddresses
$NetworkConnected

tools.name: URLParse
tools.description: Parses a URL into an association of components ("Scheme", "Domain", "Port", "Path", "Query", "Fragment", "User"), or extracts one component; URLBuild (listed) is the inverse. Use it to route requests in URLDispatcher handlers and to manipulate query parameters safely.
tools.usage:
URLParse[url]
URLParse[url, "Query"]
URLParse[url, {"Domain", "Path"}]

tools.name: URLEncode
tools.description: Percent-encodes a string for safe use in URLs (URLDecode reverses it), while URLQueryEncode / URLQueryDecode convert between association/rule lists and query strings (key=value&...). Use them when assembling URLs by hand or parsing raw query strings from HTTPRequestData.
tools.usage:
URLEncode["string"]
URLDecode["string"]
URLQueryEncode[{"k1" -> v1, "k2" -> v2}]
URLQueryEncode[<|...|>]
URLQueryDecode["k1=v1&k2=v2"]

tools.name: URLSave
tools.description: Downloads the content of a URL directly to a local file (returning the file path), with options for headers, method and cookies; URLDownload (listed) is the newer form that handles several URLs and returns File objects, and URLFetch is the legacy string-returning fetch superseded by URLRead. Check reachability first with URLRead[url, "StatusCode"].
tools.usage:
URLSave[url, "file"]
URLSave[url, "file", "Headers" -> {...}]
URLRead[url, "StatusCode"]
URLFetch[url] (* legacy *)

tools.name: URLDispatcher
tools.description: URLDispatcher[{patt1 -> handler1, ...}] deployed to the cloud routes requests by URL path (string patterns or regular expressions) to different APIFunctions, FormFunctions, Delayed pages or static content, so one CloudObject can serve a whole REST-style site; unmatched paths get a 404 unless a catch-all is given.
tools.usage:
CloudDeploy[URLDispatcher[{"/api/" ~~ __ -> APIFunction[...], "/form" -> FormFunction[...], "/" -> Delayed[homePage]}], "site"]
URLDispatcher[{RegularExpression["/items/(\\d+)"] -> handler}]

parameters.name: patt -> handler
parameters.description: Path pattern and the deployable object handling it.

tools.name: HTTPErrorResponse
tools.description: HTTPErrorResponse[code] returned from an APIFunction/Delayed/URLDispatcher body makes the cloud respond with that HTTP status (and an optional custom body), and HTTPRedirect[url] issues a redirect (302 by default, code selectable). Use them for proper REST semantics: 400 for bad input, 401/403 for auth, 404 for missing resources.
tools.usage:
HTTPErrorResponse[404]
HTTPErrorResponse[400, "body"]
HTTPErrorResponse[500, <|"Body" -> "...", "Headers" -> {...}|>]
HTTPRedirect[url]
HTTPRedirect[url, 301]
tools.example:
CloudDeploy[APIFunction[{"id" -> "Integer"}, If[KeyExistsQ[db, #id], db[#id], HTTPErrorResponse[404, "no such id"]] &, "JSON"]]
CloudDeploy[Delayed[HTTPRedirect["https://www.wolfram.com"]], "go"]

tools.name: ExportForm
tools.description: ExportForm[expr, "fmt"] specifies how a result is serialized in an HTTP response from APIFunction, Delayed or FormFunction ("JSON", "HTML", "PNG", "CSV", "XML", "String", with export options), and ResponseForm wraps the whole response including headers; GenerateHTTPResponse (listed) previews the resulting HTTPResponse locally. Use them to control content type and formatting of API output precisely.
tools.usage:
APIFunction[params, ExportForm[body[#], "JSON"] &]
ExportForm[expr, "PNG", ImageSize -> 400]
ExportForm[expr, "HTML"]
ResponseForm[expr, "fmt"]
GenerateHTTPResponse[APIFunction[...], <|"x" -> 1|>]
tools.example:
api = APIFunction[{"n" -> "Integer"}, ExportForm[Plot[Sin[#n x], {x, 0, 2 Pi}], "SVG"] &];
GenerateHTTPResponse[api, <|"n" -> 3|>]["ContentType"] (* image/svg+xml *)

tools.name: DelimitedSequence
tools.description: DelimitedSequence["type"] is an Interpreter specification for a delimited list of values (comma-separated by default, custom delimiters allowed) used in APIFunction/FormFunction parameter lists; the other specification helpers are Restricted["type", range] (bounded values), RepeatingElement, CompoundElement, AnySubset and GeoVariant. Parameters are given as "name" -> type, "name" -> type -> default, and the interpreted values appear in the body as #name; the third APIFunction argument sets the output format and HTTPRequestData exposes the raw request.
tools.usage:
APIFunction[{"n" -> "Integer", "scale" -> "Number" -> 1.0, "ids" -> DelimitedSequence["Integer"]}, body &, "JSON"]
APIFunction[{"img" -> "Image"}, ImageDimensions[#img] &]
APIFunction[{"x" -> Restricted["Real", {0, 1}]}, ... &]

tools.name: AppearanceRules
tools.description: Option of FormFunction, FormPage and AskFunction giving the presentation of a web form as an association: "Title", "Description", "SubmitLabel", "ItemLayout", "ClassName" etc.; field specifications extend APIFunction's with {"name", "Label"} -> type, "name" -> <|"Interpreter" -> ..., "Control" -> InputField, "Hint" -> "...", "Default" -> v, "Help" -> "..."|>, and FormTheme, FormLayoutFunction, PageTheme and ImageSize style the page; a list of field lists makes a multi-page form.
tools.usage:
FormFunction[{{"n", "How many?"} -> "Integer", "color" -> {"Red" -> Red, "Blue" -> Blue}}, body &, AppearanceRules -> <|"Title" -> "Demo"|>]
FormFunction[{"x" -> <|"Interpreter" -> "Number", "Hint" -> "a real number", "Default" -> 0|>}, body &, "PNG"]
FormFunction[{{page1fields}, {page2fields}}, body &] (* multi-page *)
tools.example:
CloudDeploy[FormFunction[{{"f", "Function of x"} -> "MathExpression", {"range", "x range"} -> "Number" -> 10},
   Plot[#f, {x, -#range, #range}] &, "PNG", AppearanceRules -> <|"Title" -> "Plotter", "Description" -> "Enter an expression in x"|>, FormTheme -> "Blue"], Permissions -> "Public"]

tools.name: SendMail
tools.description: Sends an email with subject, body (text, expressions, images) and attachments through the Wolfram Cloud mail relay (default) or a configured SMTP server (MailSettings / $MailSettings or explicit "Server", "UserName", "Password" options). Use it for notifications from scheduled tasks and scripts; recipients, CC/BCC and reply-to are options.
tools.usage:
SendMail["to@example.com", "body"]
SendMail["to@example.com", "subject", "body"]
SendMail[<|"To" -> {...}, "Subject" -> "...", "Body" -> {"text", plot}, "Attachments" -> {"file.pdf"}|>]
SendMail[..., "Server" -> "smtp.example.com", "UserName" -> "u", "Password" -> "p"]

parameters.name: Body
parameters.description: String or list mixing text, images and expressions.

tools.notes: MailReceiverFunction (listed) handles incoming mail sent to a cloud-generated address.

tools.name: MailServerConnect
tools.description: Connects to an IMAP mail server (Gmail, Outlook, generic) returning a MailServer object; MailFolder selects a folder, MailSearch finds messages by criteria ("From", "Subject", "Date", "Unread"...) returning MailItem objects whose properties ("Body", "Attachments", "From") can be read, and MailExecute performs actions ("MarkAsRead", "Delete", "Move"). Use them to process mailboxes programmatically.
tools.usage:
server = MailServerConnect[]
server = MailServerConnect["imap.example.com", "user", "password"]
folder = MailFolder[server, "INBOX"]
items = MailSearch[folder, <|"Unread" -> True, "From" -> "boss"|>]
items[[1]]["Body"]
MailExecute["MarkAsRead", items]
MailExecute["SaveAttachments", items, dir]

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: IMAP host (or omitted for the stored default).

tools.name: StartWebSession
tools.description: Launches a browser (Chrome or Firefox via WebDriver) controlled from Wolfram Language, returning a WebSessionObject; WebExecute performs actions ("OpenPage", "ClickElement", "TypeElement", "CapturePage", "JavascriptExecute", "LocateElements" -> WebElementObject) and WebImage captures a page screenshot. Use them for scraping dynamic sites, form automation and UI testing.
tools.usage:
session = StartWebSession[]
session = StartWebSession["Chrome"]
WebExecute[session, "OpenPage" -> url]
WebExecute[session, "LocateElements" -> "Tag" -> "a"]
WebExecute[session, {"ClickElement" -> elem, "CapturePage"}]
WebExecute[session, "JavascriptExecute" -> "return document.title"]
WebImage[url]
DeleteObject[session]

parameters.name: browser
parameters.description: "Chrome" (default) or "Firefox"; option Visible -> False for headless.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Action name -> argument; lists run several in sequence.

tools.notes: Requires a matching browser driver; WebSessions[] lists active sessions and WebWindowObject/WebElementObject represent windows and DOM elements.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description: Performs a web search (through a configured search service such as Google Custom Search or Bing, set up with ServiceConnect) returning a Dataset of results with titles, snippets and links; WebImageSearch returns image results as Image objects or thumbnails. Both require service credentials and may consume service quota.
tools.usage:
WebSearch["query"]
WebSearch["query", "Hyperlinks"]
WebSearch["query", MaxItems -> 20]
WebImageSearch["query"]
WebImageSearch["query", "Thumbnails", MaxItems -> 5]
tools.example:
WebSearch["Wolfram Language regions", "Hyperlinks", MaxItems -> 5]
WebImageSearch["Mandelbrot set", "Thumbnails", MaxItems -> 3]

tools.name: WikipediaData
tools.description: Retrieves Wikipedia article content and metadata ("ArticlePlaintext", "SummaryPlaintext", "ImageList", "Categories", "LinksRules", "Tables" ...) for a title or entity, WikipediaSearch finds articles, and WikidataData / WikidataSearch query the Wikidata knowledge base by entity and property. Free-text knowledge access complementing the curated Entity framework.
tools.usage:
WikipediaData["title"]
WikipediaData["title", "prop"]
WikipediaData[Entity["City", ...], "SummaryPlaintext"]
WikipediaSearch["query"]
WikipediaSearch["Title" -> "query", MaxItems -> 5]
WikidataData[entity, "wdprop"]
WikidataSearch["query"]

parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: Property name; Language option selects the Wikipedia edition.

tools.name: AskFunction
tools.description: AskFunction[body] builds a conversational interface: inside body, Ask["name" -> type] requests a value from the user (rendered as a web form step in the cloud or a dialog locally), AskConfirm asks yes/no, AskDisplay shows content, AskAppend collects lists, and AskedQ/AskedValue query earlier answers; deploying AskFunction with CloudDeploy produces a multi-step wizard whose questions can depend on previous answers.
tools.usage:
CloudDeploy[AskFunction[Module[{n = Ask["n" -> "Integer"]}, If[n > 10, Ask["confirm" -> "Boolean"]]; n^2]]]
Ask["name" -> "type"]
Ask[{"name", "Prompt text"} -> "type"]
AskConfirm["Continue?"]
AskDisplay[expr]
AskAppend["items" -> "String"]
AskedQ["name"]
AskedValue["name"]

parameters.name: name -> type
parameters.description: Question name and Interpreter type or control spec.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description: Sends a message through a connected messaging service - SMS/MMS via Twilio, posts to Twitter/X, Facebook, Slack-style services - using ServiceConnect credentials; SendMessage["SMS", "+1555...", "text"] is the phone form. Use it for alerts from monitoring tasks.
tools.usage:
SendMessage["SMS", "+15551234567", "text"]
SendMessage["Twitter", "text"]
SendMessage[service, "text"]
SendMessage[service, {"text", image}]

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Service name or ServiceObject from ServiceConnect.

tools.name: ServiceObject
tools.description: Represents an authenticated connection to an external web service (returned by ServiceConnect): so["Requests"] lists available requests, so["request", params] or ServiceExecute performs them, ServiceSubmit runs one asynchronously as a task, ServiceDisconnect closes it, and $ServiceCreditsAvailable reports Wolfram service credits. Dozens of built-in connections exist (OpenAI, Google, Twitter, Dropbox, Fitbit, ...) and custom ones can be defined as paclets.
tools.usage:
so = ServiceConnect["Service"]
so["Requests"]
so["Request", "param" -> value]
ServiceExecute[so, "Request", {"param" -> value}]
ServiceSubmit[ServiceRequest[so, "Request", params], HandlerFunctions -> ...]
ServiceDisconnect[so]

tools.name: $RequesterAddress
tools.description: Inside a deployed APIFunction, FormFunction or Delayed page, $RequesterAddress gives the client IP address and $RequesterWolframID the authenticated Wolfram ID (None for anonymous), while HTTPRequestData (listed) exposes the raw request keys "Method", "Headers", "Body", "BodyBytes", "Query", "PathString", "Cookies", "UserAgent". Combine them with HTTPErrorResponse for authentication and validation; $EvaluationCloudObject identifies the object being evaluated.
tools.usage:
$RequesterAddress
$RequesterWolframID
HTTPRequestData["Method"]
HTTPRequestData["Body"]
HTTPRequestData[{"Query", "PathString"}]

tools.name: CookieFunction
tools.description: Option of URLRead, URLExecute, URLDownload and HTTPRequest controlling cookie handling (Automatic uses the session cookie jar, None disables, or a function processing received cookies); $Cookies and $CookieStore hold the session cookies, and SetCookies/ClearCookies manage them. Needed for authenticated scraping sessions across several requests.
tools.usage:
URLRead[url, CookieFunction -> None]
URLRead[url, CookieFunction -> Automatic]
$Cookies
SetCookies[<|"Domain" -> "example.com", "Name" -> "session", "Content" -> "abc"|>]
ClearCookies[All]
tools.example:
URLExecute[loginUrl, {"user" -> u, "pass" -> p}, Method -> "POST"];
URLRead[protectedUrl]["Body"] (* cookies from the login are sent automatically *)

tools.name: Authentication
tools.description: Option of URLRead, URLExecute, URLDownload, HTTPRequest and ServiceConnect providing credentials: <|"Username" -> u, "Password" -> p|> (basic auth), <|"Headers" -> {"Authorization" -> "Bearer token"}|> or a SecuredAuthenticationKey (OAuth). Combine with SystemCredential to avoid hard-coding secrets in scripts.
tools.usage:
URLRead[url, Authentication -> <|"Username" -> "u", "Password" -> "p"|>]
URLRead[HTTPRequest[url, <|"Headers" -> {"Authorization" -> "Bearer " <> SystemCredential["api-token"]}|>]]
ServiceConnect["Service", Authentication -> key]

tools.name: FollowRedirects
tools.description: Option of URLRead, URLExecute, URLDownload and URLSubmit controlling whether HTTP redirects are followed (default True); the other main options are TimeConstraint (seconds before failing), VerifySecurityCertificates (True/False), Interactive (allow credential prompts) and CookieFunction. The HTTPResponse returned by URLRead has properties "StatusCode", "StatusCodeDescription", "Body", "BodyBytes", "BodyByteArray", "Headers", "ContentType", "CharacterEncoding", "Cookies" and "Version", several of which can be requested at once, and HTTPRequest[url, <|"Method" -> "POST", "Body" -> ..., "ContentType" -> ...|>] builds non-GET requests.
tools.usage:
resp = URLRead[url]
resp["StatusCode"]
resp["Body"]
URLRead[url, {"StatusCode", "Headers"}]
URLRead[HTTPRequest[url, <|"Method" -> "POST", "Body" -> ExportString[data, "JSON"], "ContentType" -> "application/json"|>]]
URLRead[url, TimeConstraint -> 10, FollowRedirects -> False]

tools.name: SocketOpen
tools.description: SocketOpen[port] opens a listening server socket (TCP by default) that SocketListen serves, and both SocketOpen and SocketConnect accept ZeroMQ socket types ("ZMQ_REQ", "ZMQ_REP", "ZMQ_PUB", "ZMQ_SUB", "ZMQ_PUSH", "ZMQ_PULL", "ZMQ_PAIR", "ZMQ_DEALER", "ZMQ_ROUTER") with tcp://, ipc:// and inproc:// addresses, giving message-framed communication with other languages' ZeroMQ bindings via SocketReadMessage/SocketWriteMessage. This is the simplest robust way to link a kernel to a Python or C++ process without WSTP.
tools.usage:
SocketOpen[port]
SocketOpen[{"host", port}, "TCP"]
rep = SocketOpen["tcp://127.0.0.1:5555", "ZMQ_REP"]
req = SocketConnect["tcp://127.0.0.1:5555", "ZMQ_REQ"]
SocketWriteMessage[req, "ping"]
ByteArrayToString[SocketReadMessage[rep]]

tools.name: URL
tools.description: URL["https://..."] wraps a string as a URL object that URLRead, URLExecute, Import, HTTPRequest, URLBuild/URLParse and SystemOpen accept and display as a clickable link; File[...] is the analogous wrapper for local paths. Using the wrapper avoids ambiguity between strings that are data and strings that are addresses.
tools.usage:
URL["https://example.com/data.csv"]
Import[URL["https://example.com/data.csv"]]
URLRead[URL["https://example.com"], "StatusCode"]
SystemOpen[URL["https://www.wolfram.com"]]

tools.name: SecuredAuthenticationKey
tools.description: Represents OAuth (1.0a/2.0) credentials for a web API, created by GenerateSecuredAuthenticationKey (listed) from consumer keys and secrets or an existing token; pass it as Authentication -> key to URLRead/URLExecute/HTTPRequest so requests are signed automatically. Store the key with SystemCredential or PersistentSymbol rather than in code.
tools.usage:
key = GenerateSecuredAuthenticationKey[<|"OAuthVersion" -> "2.0", "ClientID" -> id, "ClientSecret" -> secret, "AuthorizeEndpoint" -> ..., "AccessEndpoint" -> ...|>]
URLRead[url, Authentication -> key]
key["Properties"]

tools.name: WebElementObject
tools.description: Handle to a DOM element in a WebExecute session (returned by "LocateElements", "LocateElement") on which element actions operate: "ClickElement", "TypeElement" -> {elem, "text"}, "ElementText", "ElementAttribute", "SubmitElement", "HoverElement", "ElementImage"; WebWindowObject represents browser windows/tabs ("SetWindow", "OpenWindow") and WebSessions lists open sessions. Together with StartWebSession they give full scripted-browser control.
tools.usage:
elems = WebExecute[session, "LocateElements" -> "XPath" -> "//input[@name='q']"]
WebExecute[session, "TypeElement" -> {First[elems], "query"}]
WebExecute[session, "SubmitElement" -> First[elems]]
WebExecute[session, "ElementText" -> elem]
WebExecute[session, "ElementAttribute" -> {elem, "href"}]
win = WebExecute[session, "OpenWindow"]
WebSessions[]

tools.name: SetCookies
tools.description: Adds cookies (associations with "Domain", "Path", "Name", "Content", "ExpirationDate", "Secure") to the session cookie store used by URLRead/URLExecute/URLDownload, ClearCookies removes them (all or matching a domain) and $Cookies lists the current cookies; with CookieFunction control this supports authenticated multi-request sessions and cookie-based API tokens.
tools.usage:
SetCookies[<|"Domain" -> "example.com", "Path" -> "/", "Name" -> "session", "Content" -> "abc123"|>]
SetCookies[{cookie1, cookie2}]
$Cookies
ClearCookies[All]
ClearCookies["example.com"]
